This target turned out to have real AI features, unlike the other AI-adjacent targets in this batch (freescout/papercups/rocketchat/mattermost) — required the fuller trace, not the lighter no-AI pass.
notes: Source-verified, same pattern as chatwoot.json's Captain feature. Zammad ships real, first-party AI controllers: app/controllers/ai_assistance_controller.rb (text tools: rewrite/summarize/etc via an LLM), ai_text_tools_controller.rb, ai_agents_controller.rb, plus background jobs (ticket_ai_assistance_summarize_job.rb, ticket_ai_assistance_generate_knowledge_base_answer_job.rb, trigger_ai_agent_job.rb). Route confirmed: config/routes/ai_assistance.rb defines `scope api_path { resources :ai_assistance, only: [] { collection { post 'text_tools/:id', action: :text_tools } } }`; api_path = '/api/v1' (config/application.rb:57) -> POST /api/v1/ai_assistance/text_tools/:id. AIAssistanceController has `prepend_before_action :authenticate_and_authorize!` applied to the whole controller (real Rails auth enforcement, no bypass found) -> ai_auth_gated=true. FUNCTIONAL CAVEAT (why has_ai_surface is 'partial' not 'yes'): app/assets/javascripts/app/views/ai/missing_provider_alert.jst.eco and app/models/setting/validation/ai_provider*.rb confirm Zammad requires an admin to configure an AI provider (API key) before these features work — same functional-gating pattern as Chatwoot's Captain (config exists, auth exists, but the downstream LLM call is gated on deployment-time provider configuration not verified as present in this container). chat_ui_present is false: this is a ticketing/helpdesk product (agent-to-customer via email/tickets), not a live chat widget, and no chat-widget route was found alongside the AI controllers. soft_404_behavior not checked in this pass (focus was the AI-surface finding, which was the consequential unknown for this target).
